changelog: ONT 16S report: the Emu reference read 'Emu database (emu_db_mar2026) (emu_db_mar2026)' (label and folder both named it) and the emu command line carried that label as --db; it now reads 'Emu database (emu_db_mar2026)' and --db emu_db_mar2026. Report only. 2.35.0: Download results, Nanopore ITS (VSEARCH + UNITE) runs with the NCBI check: new option 'put the NCBI names (bacteria etc.) into the profiles'. The OTUs UNITE could not name take the name of their NCBI check (to the rank the hit supports; group only -> '<group> (unclassified)'), so the bacteria, plants and animals the fungal primers also amplified appear in the bar charts, tables, Krona, heatmap, Excel and report; the report title and method say so and keep the caveat that these reads show presence, not abundance. The zips are named ..._with_NCBI_names. main.py changed: restart. 2.34.3: 12S report: the NCBI check line no longer calls the ASVs with no NCBI hit 'mostly non-target' (with the reference gaps fixed they are mostly fish NCBI lacks). Report only. 2.34.2: fix (12S / CytB BLAST naming): MitoFish records whose species MitoFish's lineage table does not place carried no Phylum..Genus in the fish reference, so a hit on one was neither named nor recognised as a fish — a 98% Oxyurichthys (goby) ASV was 'non-target, not named' and made a sample look 83% non-target. Such records now take the ranks of their genus (at BLAST time from ids.tsv, and when the reference is built), and a MitoFish-only record the tables cannot place still counts as a fish. Re-run 12S / CytB jobs named by BLAST (Run again). blast_taxonomy.py runs as its own process: update.sh, no restart. 2.34.1: Download results and the customer report now cover 18S (PR2 / NemaBase) and COI jobs; they refused them ('the customer report covers 12S / CytB, 16S and ONT 16S runs, not COX1'). COI package text: COX1 truncLen (truncLen_cox1), merge overlap 20, the length filter, the stop-codon (NUMT) filter, LULU run or not installed, naming by VSEARCH best hit or DADA2 against MIDORI2 with its identity thresholds, MIDORI2 and VSEARCH references; read tracking reads the COX1 denoised_F / denoised_R columns; a species equal to its genus (old VSEARCH naming) is dropped. main.py changed: restart the backend. 2.34.0: Single-run reports, checked against the 3-targets eDNA project (12S / 18S PR2 / COI): (1) the method's cutadapt command shows -n 2 for runs made with v2.32.1 or later and says why; (2) COX1: the read-flow figures and step table put the length filter before chimera removal, as the pipeline runs them (the run looked as if reads came back after chimera removal); truncLen and the merge ceiling use the COX1 pair (230 / 200), not the generic 240 / 200 — the job page showed the unused pair too; (3) COX1: LULU asked for but not installed is reported as skipped, not as 'curated with LULU (0 merged)'; cox1_pipeline.R now writes whether it ran; (4) 18S: the off-target table lists the reads outside the target domain (bacteria / archaea), so its rows add up, and drops the 16S wording; a PR2 job is labelled 18S, not 18S-nema; (5) 12S BLAST: non-target reads with no name get a row with their closest hit (a sample that was 83% non-target showed none), and human DNA counted inside a vertebrate limit is said; (6) 'the 1 most abundant phylum'. Report + R script + console: update.sh, no restart, Ctrl+F5. 2.33.6: Multi-marker report: the overview table's headers (Samples, Species) no longer break mid-word. Report only: update.sh, no restart. 2.33.5: DADA2 pipeline log: 'Read lengths after trimming' now gives the median length beside the max, and the truncLen lines say 'near-max-length' reads. A 12S run whose reads were correctly trimmed to ~100 bp read as 'R1 max 287 bp ... best 185 -> 95%' (a few stray long reads), which looked like untrimmed reads. R script only. 2.33.4: fix (DADA2 pipeline log): a reference without a Kingdom/Domain rank (MIDORI2 12S / CytB / COI starts at phylum) was reported as '100% no kingdom assigned' in the taxonomy QC; the QC now counts by the reference's top rank. R script only. 2.33.3: fix (COX1 / ITS VSEARCH naming, tax_helpers.R): vsearch cuts a reference label at its first space unless --notrunclabels is given, and MIDORI2 writes the species as 'Genus epithet_taxid' — every COI job named by VSEARCH best hit (MIDORI2 too large for DADA2 on the machine) got the GENUS name in its Species column ('Ravinia Ravinia' in reports). Fixed; re-run COI jobs named by VSEARCH to get their species. Reports of such jobs now drop a species that is only its genus name (report_builder), so they show the genus instead of a false species. Multi-marker report: new section 2 'Figures side by side' — one landscape page per topic (reads per pipeline step, organism groups, genera, alpha diversity, rarefaction, PCoA), the markers' charts next to each other, each headed with marker, job, pipeline and reference; overview table no longer runs off the page; COI named by VSEARCH says so; PR2 names without '_'. R script + report only: update.sh, no restart. 2.33.2: Console: a failed or cancelled amplicon job now has Run again (it was only on completed jobs), and Run again asks which taxonomy database to use when the folder holds more than one or the one used last time is missing or empty — a COI job that stopped on the empty MIDORI2_COX1_dada2.fa.gz is re-run on MIDORI2 GenBank 273 without uploading its files again. Frontend only: update.sh, no restart, Ctrl+F5. 2.33.1: fix (COX1): a COI run stopped at taxonomy with only 'Could not read the rank structure of MIDORI2_COX1_dada2.fa.gz'. That file came from install.sh's old reference-midori.info GB256 link, which now answers with a web page saved under the reference's name. The log now says what is wrong with a reference (web page / empty / not a DADA2 trainset) and how to get the current one (download_databases.sh --only midori, MIDORI2 GenBank 273 (COI)); install.sh fetches MIDORI2 through download_databases.sh; reading the reference headers no longer fails on a stray non-UTF-8 byte (tax_helpers.R, all DADA2-family pipelines). R scripts only. 2.33.0: new: Multi-marker report. Build report with runs of different markers of the same samples ticked (e.g. 12S fish + 18S eukaryotes + COI) now gives a Multi-marker Amplicon Comparison Report instead of the Reference comparison: (1) overview per marker — target, reference and naming, samples, reads, ASVs, taxa and species named, the main organism groups each marker sees, and a sample table that shows a sample missing from a job; (2) what was found at each site — taxa per site per marker, the names site by site with the replicates they were found in (e.g. 3/3) and their mean share, and one taxa-by-site table per marker with a column for the controls that also carried a taxon. Samples are matched by name without each job's marker tag (KK-NE-1-Riaz12S = KK-NE-1_TAR = KK-NE-1_COI-XT); the site is the name without its replicate number; names ending in CT / NC / NTC / NEG / BLANK are controls. Runs of one marker keep the Reference comparison. New backend/multimarker_report.py; main.py and the Build report text. Restart the backend (main.py changed).

previous.changelog: fix (DADA2 16S / 12S / CytB / 18S, COX1, ITS Illumina pipelines): cutadapt removed only one primer per read (its default), so when the amplicon is shorter than the reads — 12S Riaz (~130 bp) or MiFish (~170 bp) in 2x300 reads, short ITS — the other primer and the sequencing adapter stayed on the 3' end (a 12S run kept 280-bp reads instead of ~95 bp, and its ASVs carried adapter). cutadapt now runs two rounds (-n 2). Re-run 12S / CytB / ITS jobs made with 2x250 or longer reads. Only the R scripts change: update.sh is enough, a running job is not affected, queued jobs pick it up. Form, 18S eukaryote / nematode: 'Species assignment' now says species come from the classifier (PR2 / 18S-NemaBase carry species as a rank) instead of the exact-match addSpecies() note of 16S; there is nothing to set for species in 18S. No backend change.

18S eukaryotes against PR2. The 18S pipeline (sidebar: '18S eukaryote / nematode', same licence key as before) runs TAReuk-type 18S V4 data against PR2 5.1.1 — algae, protists, fungi, small animals — or nematodes against 18S-NemaBase; choose the reference under Taxonomy classification (leave it on auto for NemaBase). With PR2: its nine ranks are kept (Division reported as Phylum, Supergroup and Subdivision in the tables); names PR2 gives a rank it leaves undefined ('Chlorophyta_X', '_XX') and 'Genus_sp.' become '<higher rank> unidentified' in the run's tables, figures and reports; species are written 'Genus epithet'. Reports: title '18S rRNA V4 Eukaryote Amplicon Sequencing Report', PR2 methods text and reference (Guillou et al. 2013), species note for V4, no 16S wording; Download results: '18S rRNA (eukaryotes)' with PR2 text and reference (NemaBase runs: '18S rRNA (nematodes)', Gattoni et al. 2023). Fix: the per-sample package listed UNOISE2 / UNITE / Vu et al. among the references of DADA2 runs. Install PR2 once: bash download_databases.sh --only pr2. Backend restart required. Run report: 'Analysis by group' is now a chapter of its own (heading level of Method / Result) and a report of chosen groups says at the top where the groups are compared. Alpha diversity by group says when Chao1 equals Observed (no singletons, as in Emu runs) and that with two groups Kruskal–Wallis is the Mann–Whitney test and depends only on ranks. Run report: the Archaeal community section appears only when archaeal reads were found (then listing only the samples that hold any), and Build report has 'Leave out the Archaeal community section' for Bacteria-only projects.

Report of chosen groups. Job page → Report (PDF / Word), one run: new 'Groups' — pick a grouping of the job (metadata.csv: Customise charts → Save groups, or Upload metadata) and tick the groups to report. The report then covers only those groups' samples (said at the top: N of M samples, which groups) and every number, table and figure — totals, composition, heatmap, alpha, beta, read QC — is computed from them alone; with two or more groups ticked it adds Analysis by group for them, in the order ticked: group means per rank, top genera per group, genera found only in one group, alpha diversity by group (boxes, mean ± SD, Kruskal–Wallis) and beta diversity by group (PERMANOVA, within / between dissimilarity). 'All samples (no grouping)' gives the whole-run report as before. Backend restart required.

Groups set after the run. (1) Run report (Report PDF / Word): new 'Analysis by group' from the job's metadata.csv as it is now — the 'group'/'Group' column, else the first other grouping column (e.g. 'Type'); metadata.csv now wins over the groups given with the run. It gives the groups and their samples; taxa by group (ten top genera per group with how many of its samples hold each, genera found only in one group, mean composition per group at phylum, genus and species); alpha diversity by group (boxes with the samples as dots, mean ± SD, Kruskal–Wallis per index); beta diversity by group (PERMANOVA on Bray–Curtis, 999 permutations, computed in the report so it follows the current groups; mean dissimilarity within and between groups). The PCoA is coloured by group, and on many-sample runs the landscape bar charts are ordered by group with a labelled bracket per group. (2) Customise charts → Groups: 'Group by name' — split the sample names at a separator and fill every sample's group from the chosen part(s) (e.g. part 2 of D1K2_W_HI_R1 = W). Backend restart required. (3) Customise charts → Groups is now a group manager: '＋ Create group' (then tick its samples), each group a box of sample chips — drag a sample onto another group, or press Manage for a list with a search box and 'Tick all shown' (type D1K1, tick all); Rename / Delete per group; a sample is in one group of a grouping at a time. (4) 'Upload metadata…': a CSV / TSV / Excel file prepared elsewhere (e.g. by BI, groups set by the customer) becomes the job's metadata.csv — the sample-name column is found by its values and matched ignoring case and punctuation, a running-number column is dropped, every other column becomes a grouping, the old file is kept as metadata.csv.bak-<time>, and the console lists samples that did not match either way. Saving groups also stores the chosen grouping in edit_charts/settings.json, which the run report and 'Re-render in R' follow.

Run report (Build report → Report PDF / Word) for runs with many samples (more than 24, e.g. the 89-sample coral run): the sample-wise figures are printed on A4 landscape pages, at most 45 samples to a page (89 = 45 + 44), with vertical sample labels — stacked bars of every rank (same taxa and colours on every part), the genus heatmap (rows clustered over the whole run, one colour scale; samples in the order of the bars), alpha diversity (Observed + Chao1, Shannon + Simpson, one landscape page each) and the PCoA (names printed where they do not overlap, no 89-name legend). The read-step and rarefaction charts drop their sample legends, the UPGMA tree fits one page, and the Bray–Curtis matrix is not printed above 40 samples (the report says where it is). The Word file gets matching landscape sections. Runs of up to 24 samples are unchanged. Backend restart required.

Download results (VSEARCH / ITS): the NCBI-check tables of the report get their own column widths — one line per OTU instead of names broken mid-word over three pages; identity and coverage in one column; the 'Named' list of each group with most reads first. Backend restart required.

VSEARCH OTU runs: the NCBI check of unassigned OTUs is now its own step on the job page (Step 10/10, after the tables and plots; runs without it show 9 steps) and is OFF unless 'NCBI check of unassigned OTUs' is ticked in the form, because it sends those sequences to NCBI. A finished run can still be checked with python3 backend/ncbi_unassigned.py --run_dir backend/results/<job>. Backend restart required.

VSEARCH OTU runs (Nanopore ITS and other VSEARCH runs): NCBI check of unassigned OTUs, on by default ('NCBI check of unassigned OTUs' in the form; needs internet). The OTUs the reference cannot name (no phylum, e.g. bacterial or plant DNA the ITS primers amplified off-target) are BLASTed against NCBI nt (megablast, URL API, batches of 50, most-read 200 OTUs), the closest record's lineage is read from NCBI taxonomy, and each OTU is named to genus at >=95% identity, family >=90%, phylum >=80% over >=80% of the OTU when the equally good records agree, otherwise only its group (Bacteria, Archaea, Fungi, Plants, Animals, Other eukaryotes, Viruses, No NCBI match). Written as ncbi_unassigned.tsv/.json in the run folder; Download results adds 2.Taxonomy/NCBI/unassigned_otus_ncbi.tsv and a report section (groups with % of the sample's reads, the OTUs with their closest record) stating that these reads show what is present, not how much, and that a bacterial profile needs 16S; the run report gets the same section per sample. If NCBI cannot be reached the run still finishes and the reports say so. A finished run can be checked afterwards: python3 backend/ncbi_unassigned.py --run_dir backend/results/<job>, then build Download results again. Backend restart required.

VSEARCH OTU runs (Nanopore ITS, ONT 16S via VSEARCH): new setting 'Merge OTU variants' (off / 97% / 98% / 99%, default off). After UNOISE, OTUs within that identity of a more abundant one are merged into it (vsearch --cluster_size, abundance-sorted, so the most abundant sequence stays the centroid and names the OTU); nanopore errors otherwise leave near-copies of an abundant OTU as OTUs of their own, which the ITS species floor (98.41%) then names only to genus. The UNOISE set is kept as otus_unoise.fasta and which OTU went where as otu_merge.uc; the reports say it was done and how many OTUs there were before. On PGU-ITS (ITS1, ONT) 97% gives 75 -> 52 OTUs, the Nannizziopsis variants joining SV001. Backend restart required.

fix (VSEARCH OTU runs, e.g. Nanopore ITS): (1) cutadapt removed only one primer per read (its default), so about half of the reads kept the forward primer and the bases before it; it now runs two rounds (-n 2) when both primers are given (single-end and paired), and accepts the last 7 bases of the forward primer at a read start (OTUs no longer begin with a primer stub such as AACCTGCGG). Re-run a Nanopore ITS job made before 2.26.2 to get the cleaner OTUs. (2) Download results: 2.Taxonomy/outfiles/otus.fasta is named by the tables' SV numbers (>SV001 OTU_1 reads=… species) instead of the pipeline's OTU_n;size=… ids. Backend restart required.

Download results for Nanopore ITS (VSEARCH + UNITE) runs: per sample folders 1.QcReads (NanoPlot, read tracking, filtered reads), 2.Taxonomy (tables per rank, BIOM, the sample's OTU centroid sequences otus.fasta, bar charts, heatmap, Krona), 3.Diversity, 4.Tables and Report_<sample>.pdf/.docx 'Fungal ITS1 amplicon sequencing report' describing chopper, cutadapt, VSEARCH dereplication / reference chimera check / UNOISE3 / read mapping and UNITE naming with the fungal identity floors (Vu et al. 2019); references VSEARCH, UNOISE, UNITE, Vu et al., NanoPack2 — no Emu / DADA2 text. The VSEARCH pipeline records its read-prep settings in summary.json. Run report: read tracking of nanopore VSEARCH runs in the order the steps ran (QC, then primers); ITS copy-number note instead of the rRNA-operon one. The web page shows the server's reason when a request is refused (it showed only 'HTTP 400'). Backend restart required.

Nanopore ITS (fungi). (1) ITS1 / ITS2 with Sequencer = ONT (or VSEARCH OTUs) now runs the VSEARCH OTU pipeline with the UNITE reference instead of its_pipeline.R, which is DADA2 paired-end only and stopped on 'No R2 FASTQ files': chopper, cutadapt on both strands (untouched Illumina defaults -e 0.1 -O 3 become -e 0.2 -O 10 for ONT), reference chimera check, UNOISE, every read mapped back, UNITE names cut by the fungal identity floors of Vu et al. 2019 (species 98.41, genus 94.3, family 88.5, order 81.2, class 80.9, phylum 75%; taxonomy search at 75%). (2) The ITS form offers 'MinKNOW folders — merge per barcode' (folder path or upload) and a read-length window (default 100-900 bp after primers). (3) MinKNOW / Guppy chunk names fastq_runid_<run id>_<n>[_<m>] are grouped into one sample (named after their folder), for ONT 16S, ONT WGS and ITS alike; the VSEARCH pipeline merges a sample's chunk files. (4) UNITE headers (Name|Acc|SH|reps|k__…;s__…) are parsed; 'unidentified' ranks left blank; unassigned OTUs of an ITS run no longer default to Kingdom 'Bacteria'. (5) Report: ITS identity floors and Vu et al. 2019 / NanoPack2 cited for Nanopore ITS. Backend restart required.

12S / CytB fish eDNA. (1) BLAST naming works on Python 3.14: blast_taxonomy.py stopped at start-up ('badly formed help string' — a bare % in an argparse help text), so every 12S/CytB run silently kept the DADA2 names; a test now scans every backend script for this. (2) Run report (Report PDF / Word) of a BLAST-named run: the method describes BLASTn naming (MIDORI2 + MitoFish, ties within 0.5%, identity thresholds, fish limit, NCBI check) instead of the naive Bayesian classifier; a new section gives fish / non-target / no-match reads per sample, the fish taxa named (rank reached, best-hit identity, samples) — fish whose best hit is below the class threshold are shown as not in the reference instead of by a distant species name — the main non-target taxa, human DNA, and the NCBI agreement; config rows for the BLAST settings; BLAST+ and MitoFish references. (3) CytB runs are titled CytB; no Bacteria/Archaea sentence, V3-V4/16S species note or rRNA-operon note on 12S/CytB; MIDORI2 taxid suffixes removed for every MIDORI2 reference; a genus is reported 'within' its own phylum. (4) DADA2 runs: samples subsampled to 100,000 reads before denoising are named and the drop at that step is explained as the cap, not read loss. Backend restart required. (5) Fish report details: a phylum-only name is labelled as a distant best hit only when the identity really is below the class threshold (otherwise 'cut to phylum: conflicting hits'); the flagged-for-checking list counts repeats; the composition text says what a phylum-level BLAST name means; a sample that lost most reads at chimera removal is told so (PCR, not sequencing quality). (6) Fish share counts only reads identified at the class threshold (80%) or more; reads whose best hit is a fish below it are a separate column ('fish-like, unconfirmed'), not counted as fish. (7) A fish named by NCBI only (no local hit) is a target: blast_taxonomy.py now marks it so, and the report counts such ASVs of older runs as fish instead of 'no match'. Non-target Chordata cut to phylum because local and NCBI disagree are labelled so. (8) NCBI check: an ASV whose local best hit is non-target (e.g. human) is no longer cut to phylum and flagged when NCBI, searched for fish only, returns a fish record of the same identity — such a record is contaminated with human DNA (seen: Parablennius sanguinolentus records matching human CytB at 97-99%); the local name stands ('outside_limit'). A fish clearly closer than the non-target hit still overrules it and is flagged.

ONT 16S: Resume run. A run cut off part-way (server restart, Windows Update, power cut) shows 'Resume run' in Job Detail: same input files and recorded settings, same results folder; samples Emu already finished are reused (their alignment SAM files removed), QC/trimmed reads on disk are reused, only the remaining samples run, then tables and plots. Nothing is deleted; pipeline.log keeps the interrupted run above the resumed one. Per-sample outputs are now written under a temporary name and renamed when complete. Also carries the pending 2.25.0 fixes: Emu SAM files deleted after each sample, read-quality panel single mode for ONT, DB picker shows the folder. Backend restart required.

ONT WGS customer package + read-based taxonomy + TYGS dDDH + Download results for every pipeline. (1) ONT WGS: per sample a package laid out like the lab's: folders 1.QcReads, 2.Assembly, 3.Completeness, 4.Taxonomy (TYGS, Read-based Taxonomy, Contig-based Taxonomy, 16S, MLST, Phylogeny), 5.ANI, 6.Annotation, 7.AMR (AMRFinderPlus, VFDB, PlasmidFinder, MOB-suite), 8.readsMappingToRef, and Report_<sample>.pdf / .docx ('Whole genome sequencing report', no cover, each section ending 'Results <folder>'); only steps that ran and only our tools are named. (2) Read-based taxonomy (new WGS step, also 'Add read-based taxonomy' on a finished job through the queue): Kraken2+Bracken (existing Kraken2 DB), Centrifuger (RefSeq 2023 index; Centrifuge p+h+v when WSL has < 60 GB RAM) and GOTTCHA2 2.5 nanopore mode (RefSeq-GTDB multi-domain+ fast DB) on the filtered reads; heatmap in the report; a missing tool or DB = one column less with a note. Install: bash setup_wgs.sh --readtax --db-dir /mnt/e/ngamp-db/readtax (refuses a download that would leave < 20 GB free). (3) dDDH from TYGS: Genome report → 'Assembly for TYGS', upload it yourself at tygs.dsmz.de (the genome goes to DSMZ), paste the result link → Import: Table 4.1, the dDDH table (d0/d4/d6) and the TYGS trees; other genomes of the same TYGS job are left out; an unfinished TYGS job is re-checked at most every 30 min. (4) Download results (Job Detail, all pipelines): tick samples (filter box for long runs), one zip per sample (default) or one zip. One standard for every pipeline: numbered folders + Report_<sample>.pdf/.docx laid out like the WGS report (no cover, numbered sections, each ending 'Results <folder>'). Amplicon (ONT 16S, 16S, 12S/CytB): 1.QcReads (read tracking, NanoPlot or FastQC/fastp, DADA2 quality profiles, filtered reads optional), 2.Taxonomy (tables per rank, ASV FASTA, BIOM, bar charts, Top 50 heatmap, Krona, Emu's own table, BLAST/NCBI check), 3.Diversity (alpha, rarefaction), 4.Tables (Excel); a step that did not run leaves NOT_AVAILABLE.txt; built through the job queue with progress, zips written to disk (results/<job>/packages). 'Everything (.zip)' is now written to disk instead of memory. Backend restart required.
fix: Customer report Top 50 heatmap (microbiomeutilities): rows read 'SV001:Brevundimonas sp. DS20' instead of the taxon name printed twice. Backend restart required.

fix: (1) Customer report (ONT 16S): read quality given two ways — over whole reads, and without the first 60 bases, the way MinKNOW scores a read (so it can be compared with the MinKNOW report). (2) Top 50 heatmap: microbiomeutilities is called without column clustering (one sample per report), so it no longer falls back to pheatmap. (3) The R figure log is kept beside each package (<sample>_customer_report.plots.log) for checking. Backend restart required.

fix: (1) Customer report (ONT 16S): mean read quality is now computed from each read's mean error rate, as MinKNOW and NanoPlot do — the mean of the Phred numbers overstated it (Q38.6 instead of about Q21.7). Rebuild a customer report made with 2.24.0 to get the right value. (2) setup_amplicon_report.sh installs gghalves (GitHub) and Bioconductor microbiome before microbiomeutilities, and says when venneuler needs Java. Backend restart required.

Customer report per sample. (1) Job Detail → Build report → Customer report: tick the samples and pick 'One report per sample' (default) or 'One report for the chosen samples'. Per sample = one zip (<sample>_customer_report.zip: Word + PDF, R figures, tables, Excel, BIOM, FASTA, filtered reads) built from a view of the run holding only that sample — no name, taxon, count or figure of another sample, NCBI counts and SV numbers recomputed for it; for runs whose samples belong to different customers. (2) The customer report now covers 16S Illumina (DADA2) and ONT 16S (Emu) as well as 12S / CytB, each with its real methods: ONT = read statistics (+ NanoPlot when installed), Chopper Q / length filter, cutadapt primer removal, Emu with its database and minimum abundance. (3) emu_pipeline.py records its QC / trimming settings in summary.json. Install NanoPlot (optional): bash setup_amplicon_report.sh. (4) Job queue: one job at a time by default and a 3-minute pause after each job ends (finished, failed or cancelled) before the next starts — both in Settings and saved across restarts. New Queue page: what runs, the pause countdown, the waiting jobs in order with ↑ / ↓ / To front / Cancel; the order is saved. Jobs still waiting when the backend restarts go back in the queue in their order (after one pause) instead of failing. Changing 'Jobs at once' while jobs wait no longer lets more jobs run than set. Backend restart required.

12S / CytB fish eDNA. (1) CytB: preset 'CytB fish (L14912 / H15149)' on the 12S / CytB pipeline (12S licence), MIDORI2 CytB trainset. (2) Species names by BLASTn (12S/CytB, on by default for new 12S runs; DADA2 kept beside): reference built from the newest MIDORI2 (GenBank, Leray et al. 2022) + newest MitoFish (Zhu et al. 2023), with records MitoFish judges mislabelled (heterospecific) and records with >1% ambiguous bases removed; limited to fish (NCBI: txid 7898 ray-finned + txid 7777 cartilaginous) or vertebrates (txid 7742); a sequence filed under several species is kept once and named to their shared rank; up to 5000 hits per ASV so ties are never cut off; lowest common rank of ties within 0.5%, never a species below 98.5% (genus 95, family 90, order 85, class 80); human and other non-target ASVs keep their real names; every ASV checked against NCBI nt (BLAST URL API), disagreements and NCBI species ties cut to the shared rank and flagged; a failed NCBI batch keeps the finished ones (its ASVs: not checked). Install: bash download_databases.sh --fishmito. (3) Customer report (Job Detail → Build report → Customer report): the lab's per-sample format, same headings and figure placement, cover left blank for the BI team, no company name; Word + PDF + SampleN_ folders (Box plot, bar charts per rank, Top 50 heatmap, Krona, rarefaction, alpha, outfiles, BIOM, Excel per sample) as one zip; FastQC, fastp, cutadapt, DADA2, BLASTn, phyloseq, ggplot2, microbiomeutilities, Krona, vegan. Install: bash setup_amplicon_report.sh. The report states only what the run did (pool, rm.phix, fastp as a check, BLAST skipped, unknown raw counts, samples the pipeline dropped). Backend restart required.

setup_shotgun.sh --func: the conda env ngamp-func was created with python 3.10, but bioconda builds humann 3.9 for python 3.12 only, so 'humann_databases' stopped with "No module named 'humann'". The env now uses python 3.12, is checked by importing humann and metaphlan, and a broken env is rebuilt. Nothing else changes; no backend restart needed.
